beats.text: At seventy-eight, she saw her community's rule accepted.
Forty years of teaching had grown into a community.
beats.scene: A plain stone seventeenth-century convent house with steep roofs and a small bell tower in deep winter snow at dusk, warm light in a few small windows, a path of footprints leading to the door, mist, hard side light. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.

beats.text: The sisters kept their way: teachers among the people, not behind walls.
She died in Montreal on the twelfth of January, 1700.
beats.scene: A wide frozen river at night under a heavy sky, a small fort-town far away on its bank with a single candle glowing in one window, deep snow, hard low light. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.

beats.text: The Vatican biography says her last act was a prayer for a sick young sister.
In 1982, the Church declared her a saint.
beats.scene: The interior of a bare stone chapel, a shaft of hard light from a high window falling on a small wooden altar with one lit candle and a plain statue of the Virgin, dust drifting, deep shadows. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.

beats.text: Her sisters still teach today, in several countries.
Saint Marguerite Bourgeoys, pray for us.
beats.scene: A plain wooden cross on a bare stone wall with one candle burning below it, hard side light, deep black shadows, a thin rising line of candle smoke. Skewed angular painted-set architecture. No people.
